replies.text: Yet another video where i'm gobsmacked by folks stupidity.  Are some Americans a bit retarded? Surely even a low level of intelligence, would show when you just can't afford the debt/ repayments. I'm not sure about the rest of Europe, but in Ireland it isn't as easy to get credit cards, or indeed credit. A person has to be over 18, have a verifiable regular job. The lending institution needs proof you can afford it, and checks your credit history. You need to prove that on top of all your regular expenses, you can justify them giving you a credit card. What ye call pay day loans, are short term loans here. Not payable on next payment, generally over a period of months. While the interest rate is high, its not like in usa and its capped by the government. Unfortunately BNPL arrived, and is particularly popular with the under 40 age group. Not a new concept here, but certainly the way its marketed is. Some very generous terms on big ticket items, so I can see why its so attractive.  But what happened to save now, buy later? Yes, we have our fair share of eejits here too, but not the same access to credit. With a smaller population, the number of credit cards available is very limited. Which can only be a good thing.
